newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italy's Olivetti stays deep in the red in 96.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italy's Olivetti stays deep in the red in 96.

text.p: Italy's Olivetti stayed deep in the red in 1996 as the ailing information technology group reported on Wednesday that its second half sales slumped as uncertainty over the group's future had gripped the whole company.
The group said its pre-tax loss would be around 800 billion lire ($497 million) for 1996, while its annual sales slumped 16 percent to 8.27 trillion lire from levels seen in 1995.

In a statement following the company's first 1997 board meeting at its headquarters in Ivrea near Turin, northwest Italy, Olivetti said second half 1996 sales crashed 21 percent highlighting the uncertainty hanging over the group's future.

Olivetti has seen three chief executives during 1996, wide-ranging management changes and the departure of its chairman Carlo De Benedetti as it has tried to reverse a series of losses at the group which has not made a profit since 1990.

The Olivetti statement said that the 800 billion lire of pretax losses included 200 billion lire of losses from its 35.5 percent owned mobile phone group Omnitel, which Olivetti said was in line with the company's own forecasts.

The overall loss was largely in line with analysts' estimates, but they were concerned at the lack of details with no divisional breakdown of profits and losses and no clear indication of restructuring or write-downs across the company.
"They seem to have got cash flow under control, but it is very worrying what might be happening to operating profits for the different Olivetti companies," said one analyst.

The group turned in a net loss of 1.589 trillion lire in 1995 after restructuring charges of 1.123 trillion, but at the operating level it made a 114 billion lire profit. However, in the first half of 1996, the group slipped to an operating loss of 81 billion lire and a pretax loss of 440.2 billion lire.

The group said its net debt at end-December 1996 was 2.250 trillion lire against 2.916 trillion lire at the end-November, and had fallen from over three trillion at end-August due to an asset disposal plan and stringent control over costs.
The company warned these figures were indicative and may undergo variations during the consolidation of the financial positions of more than 200 companies in the Olivetti group.

It said the improvement was highlighted by a financial surplus of 666 billion lire in December which came from disposals and an improvement in operating cash flow, offset slightly by 24 billion lire of restructuring charges.
The group said that a sale of a 5.6 percent stake in Omnitel and U.S. venture capital interests had netted 531 billion lire while its cash flow improved 159 billion lire.

"Following the preliminary agreement for the sale of the personal computer business, Olivetti now has a structure that is in line with the competitive and market scenario and consistent with its strategic profile," said chief executive Roberto Colaninno in the statement.
He reiterated that the group intended to focus on telecoms, information technology and office products, and that management will pay close attention to cash flows and operating costs.

Analysts said the group's personal computer company, sold earlier this month, would have made losses for 1996 but they were concerned Olivetti's core business Olivetti Solutions, formerly systems and services, could have slipped into the red.

Olivetti shares ended off 0.14 percent at 651 lire in an overall lower Milan stock market, after they had hit a record low of 435 lire in October just one month after Colaninno took over when uncertainty over the group was at its height. ($1=1,611 lire)
